findings: Noise rate (0.88) is high: 17 of 25 findings are false or not applicable, indicating significant agent output noise despite passing other thresholds.
Final outcome improvement rate is 0.0; agent activity has not yet translated into measurable outcome improvements in the value-gate fixture.
Current human intervention rate (0.0833) exceeds the long-term target maximum (0.01) by over 8x, acknowledged in limitations but unresolved.
Agent operational value and community self-maintenance are both marked false in current-state.json, confirming pilot passage does not equate to demonstrated operational value.
Only one independent model lineage (qwen3.7-max) was used across seven sessions, limiting generalizability of pilot results.
Maintenance report identifies a source revision drift but proposes no automatic correction, correctly deferring to human authority.
No external participants, adopters, or public authorization exist; all activity remains internal and synthetic.
required_corrections: Reduce agent noise rate below an acceptable threshold (e.g., <0.3) before claiming community value; 68% false/not-applicable findings is unsustainable for external consumption.
Address the gap between current human intervention rate (0.0833) and long-term target (0.01) with a concrete remediation plan or formally accept the current rate as pilot-stage appropriate.
Demonstrate at least one measurable final outcome improvement in the value-gate fixture to validate that agent activity produces tangible value, not just conformance.
optional_suggestions: Introduce at least one additional independent model lineage to strengthen the generalizability claim of pilot results.
Consider adding a noise-rate threshold to threshold_results to enforce a maximum acceptable noise level alongside other quality gates.
Document a clear transition criteria from 'pilot passed' to 'operational value demonstrated' to avoid ambiguity in future state assessments.
uncertainty: Whether the 0.88 noise rate is inherent to the agent's current capability or an artifact of the specific five-task fixture design.
Whether the frozen value-gate fixture is representative of real-world tasks where outcome improvement might be more achievable.
The actual impact of single-lineage model testing on result reliability cannot be quantified without cross-model comparison data.
limitations: Review is based solely on self-reported JSON artifacts from an isolated session; no independent external verification has occurred.
No access to the actual agent outputs or task execution traces; assessment relies on aggregated metrics only.
Pilot results are synthetic and internal; they do not constitute evidence of external community value or adoption readiness.
The 99% autonomy target is explicitly not claimed and remains a long-term aspiration, not a current measured fact.
